args.task: Search news or press releases about Council Member Lincoln Restler allocating discretionary or capital funding to District 33 parks in 2026.

result:
* Following a June 25, 2026, land use vote on the Monitor Point rezoning in Brooklyn, Council Member Lincoln Restler and Council Speaker Julie Menin announced a public-private partnership agreement ([NYC Council Press: Monitor Point Rezoning](https://council.nyc.gov/press/2026/06/25/3147/)).
* The agreement secured **$300,000 annually** dedicated to the long-term maintenance of Bushwick Inlet Park ([NYC Council Press: Monitor Point Rezoning](https://council.nyc.gov/press/2026/06/25/3147/)).
* The deal also secured an administration commitment to finally complete the long-promised Bushwick Inlet Park and create over 1 acre of new waterfront open space connecting the Greenpoint waterfront to the park ([NYC Council Press: Monitor Point Rezoning](https://council.nyc.gov/press/2026/06/25/3147/)).
* In tree-related investments, District 33's office invested over $1.5 million in trees through capital allocations and donations to the District 33 Tree Fund, with thousands of new trees scheduled to be planted by the end of 2026 ([Lincoln Restler: Tree Plan](https://www.lincolnrestler.nyc/tree-plan)).
* The office secured $285,000 via private contributions and discretionary Council funding directed toward expanding tree beds, installing tree guards, and adding tree planters through a partnership with the North Brooklyn Parks Alliance ([North Brooklyn Parks Alliance: District 33 Tree Fund](https://support.nbkparks.org/campaign/district-33-tree-fund/c440038)).

Joint Statement from Speaker Julie Menin and Council Member Lincoln Restler on the Vote to Approve Monitor Point Rezoning
June 25, 2026
CITY HALL, NY –
Today, New York City Council Speaker Julie Menin and Council Member Lincoln Restler issued the following statement after the Subcommittee on Zoning and Franchises and Committee on Land Use voted to approve the Monitor Point rezoning in Brooklyn:
“Today marks a major victory in the fight to make New York City more affordable. The Council took a significant step toward approving Monitor Point, a transformative majority-affordable housing development in Greenpoint that will create hundreds of permanently affordable homes, including supportive housing, deeply affordable apartments for seniors, and homes for working families.
“At the Council’s insistence, the proposal was strengthened to increase the share of permanently affordable housing from 25% to 50%, nearly tripling the number of affordable units to more than 660. We also secured a commitment from the Administration to finally complete the long-promised Bushwick Inlet Park.
“This project reflects what is possible when we demand what New Yorkers deserve: more affordable housing, dynamic green spaces, and meaningful investments in public transit and other community benefits that make neighborhoods more livable. The City Council, the MTA, and the Mamdani Administration contributed to this public-private partnership on the waterfront.
